chunks: And (many a one) there is among them who says: "Allow me (to stay back at home), and put me not on trial." Surely they have put themselves on trial already, and Hell will enclose the unbelievers from all sides.

key_terms.الْفِتْنَة: Trial, testing, or tribulation; here referring to the act of staying behind which became a test of faith and a cause of spiritual loss.
key_terms.جَهَنَّمَ: Hell; the place of punishment for the disbelievers.
key_terms.سَقَطُوا: They fell; indicating their spiritual downfall or loss of merit due to their failure in the trial.
key_terms.لَمُحِيطَةٌ: Enclosing or encompassing; describing how Hell surrounds the disbelievers with no escape.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Ala fi al-fitnat saqatu' in Surah At-Tawbah?
ai.summary: In the context of the Battle of Tabuk, this verse critiques the hypocrites (Munafiqun) who requested exemption, highlighting that their refusal to strive was itself a test (fitnah) that caused their spiritual downfall. Shia scholarship often interprets 'fitnah' here as the trial of sincerity, where their excuse became the very cause of their damnation, emphasizing that divine punishment will encompass all disbelievers.
